description:
Incident bot + diagnostics improvements is a cross-functional reliability initiative to reduce incident MTTR and repeat incidents by upgrading Redwood Inference’s automated incident context gathering. The bot (primarily used in #incidents and #eng-oncall) will be enhanced to automatically attach: (1) recent deploy context (service/version, rollout phase, canary status, related PRs), (2) customer/tenant-safe config diffs (feature flags, routing policy, quota/rate-limit, model pins) with redaction, and (3) saturation signals (GPU utilization, KV cache pressure, queue depth, scheduler/backpressure indicators, regional capacity) plus deep links to dashboards and traces.

Goals:
- Reduce time-to-triage and time-to-mitigation for common incident classes (deploy regressions, misconfig, regional capacity/saturation).
- Standardize “first 5 minutes” incident context so on-call has consistent evidence, fewer ad-hoc queries, and better handoffs.
- Improve graceful degradation decisions during incidents by surfacing relevant routing/fallback configuration and capacity signals.

In-scope deliverables:
- Incident bot v2 Slack experience (context “cards”, interactive actions, retries/timeouts, feature flag rollout).
- New/updated backend endpoints/services to export deploy metadata, config diff retrieval with redaction, and telemetry query aggregation with caching/guardrails.
- Observability updates: new metrics for saturation signals, dashboards, and alert tuning aligned to SLOs/error budgets.
- Runbooks/standards for incident context collection and access/audit requirements.

Out of scope:
- Full incident management process overhaul, major status page tooling changes, and long-term data warehouse re-architecture.

Key stakeholders:
- SRE (incident process owner, paging hygiene, MTTR tracking): Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton, Aisha Bello, Jacob Stein.
- Platform control plane + routing (config/policy, permissions, graceful degradation): Priya Natarajan, Ethan Park, Mina Haddad, Ravi Menon, Jordan Lee.
- Telemetry/observability (signals, dashboards, query performance/cardinality): Logan Wright, Allison Grant, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson.
- Release engineering (deploy metadata, rollout linkage): Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer.
- Product (rollouts/console deep links, success metrics): Marissa Cole, Paula Mendes.
- Support/CS (customer-impact feedback loops via Jira): ties to SUP tickets and escalations.

Phases / timeline (typical 6–10 weeks):
1) Discovery + requirements: baseline MTTR, top failure modes, signal inventory, data access constraints.
2) Data-source plumbing: deploy metadata export, config diff API, saturation metrics standardization.
3) Bot UX + reliability: Slack rendering/actions, timeouts/retries, caching, rate limiting, redaction.
4) Rollout: feature-flagged beta in limited on-call rotations/regions, then broad rollout.
5) Measurement: MTTR deltas, “context completeness” score, on-call feedback, follow-up tickets.

Constraints:
- Strict tenant/customer data handling: config diffs must be redacted; access must be audited.
- Telemetry cardinality and query cost must be bounded; bot queries must degrade gracefully.
- Bot must remain usable during partial outages (timeouts, fallback links, cached context).

files.description: Primary design doc for Incident Bot v2: goals, architecture, data sources (deploy/config/telemetry), Slack UX, caching, rate limits, failure modes, and rollout plan.
ADR documenting which internal services the bot can call, permission model, audit requirements, and why these sources were chosen vs alternatives.
Standard for incident context payloads (required fields, naming conventions, deep-link formats), plus guidance to keep queries bounded and signals actionable.
Updated on-call playbook: how to use bot context cards in the first 5 minutes, how to verify deploy/config diffs, and escalation paths when context is missing.
Runbook explaining how to interpret recent deploy context and config diffs, common pitfalls (staged rollouts, partial propagation), and manual fallback commands.
GPU saturation triage runbook mapping bot-reported saturation signals to likely causes (batching, queueing, KV cache pressure) and mitigation steps.
Definition of standardized saturation metrics across hosted/dedicated pools (thresholds, aggregation, labels) and how they feed incident diagnostics.
Documentation linking common SLO burn patterns (latency/5xx/streaming disconnects) to the bot’s recommended diagnostic signals and dashboards.
Spec for exporting deploy metadata (service, image SHA, rollout phase, canary results) in a machine-readable format consumable by incident-bot.
Restricted doc describing audit log events for bot access to config/telemetry, retention requirements, and review procedure for compliance.
Postmortem used to justify the project: missing deploy context increased MTTR; includes follow-up action items that map to bot v2 features.
Kickoff notes and working agenda: stakeholders, top incident classes, initial success metrics, open questions, and owners.
Spreadsheet-style inventory of desired signals (deploy/config/saturation), current source-of-truth, query cost estimates, and gaps.
Working metrics sheet: baseline MTTR by incident type, target reductions, measurement plan, and experiment design for beta rollout.
Draft JSON schema for incident context payloads and card rendering: required/optional fields, redaction rules, and versioning approach.
Platform team working notes for a config diff endpoint: data model, authorization, redaction strategy, and edge cases (rollbacks, partial writes).
Notes on how to join deploy events to services/regions/tenants, plus guidance for canary vs full rollout representation.
Examples of Slack incident threads with proposed context cards and interactive actions (expand diff, open dashboard links, copy commands).
Early PRD draft: user stories for on-call/SRE, deep link requirements into Console, and success metrics tied to reliability program KPIs.
Implementation ticket for a “Recent deploys” card: rollout phase, canary health, and links to relevant GitHub PRs/commits.
Ticket to build config diff retrieval + redaction: secret detection, allowlist fields, and customer-safe rendering in Slack.
Ticket to integrate saturation signals (GPU util, queue depth, KV cache pressure) into bot context and define thresholds.
Ticket to generate error budget burn links and embed them into incident context cards (per-region/per-route).
Reliability ticket for Slack interactions: ack deadlines, retries, idempotency, and graceful degradation when upstream queries time out.
Ticket to implement least-privilege service scopes for deploy/config/telemetry access, including audit events and break-glass procedure.
Ticket to add caching and request coalescing for telemetry queries to keep bot response times predictable during incidents.
Ticket for feature-flagged rollout plan, beta cohorts (SRE rotation only), and rollback criteria.
Ticket to add load shedding for diagnostics under high error rates: fallback to cached context + links instead of live queries.
Ticket to integrate postmortem action items with bot output (auto-suggest likely causes, link to prior similar incidents).
PM ticket capturing user stories (on-call, platform, support) and defining success metrics (MTTR reduction, context completeness, adoption).
PM/ProdOps KPI tracking ticket: target MTTR improvements and reporting cadence for the broader reliability program.
Design ticket for context card layout in Slack: hierarchy, truncation, drill-down behavior, and accessibility.
Design ticket for how redacted fields are displayed (warnings, safe previews, and how to request elevated access if needed).
Documentation work ticket: update runbooks, add troubleshooting steps for missing context, and publish standards/ADR references.
PR in incident-bot repo adding a deploy context card (recent deploys, canary status, commit SHA) and Slack rendering changes.
PR implementing config diff fetcher integration and basic diff formatting for Slack output.
PR adding saturation queries (GPU/queue/KV cache) and summarizing thresholds in the bot’s incident context payload.
PR improving Slack UX for large diffs/signals (modal pagination) and adding caching for repeated thread interactions.
PR adding redaction rules (secret patterns, allowlists) and tests to ensure no sensitive fields leak into Slack.
PR introducing feature flags and cohort targeting for v2 diagnostics output with safe rollback.
PR adding end-to-end tests for #incidents interactions, including timeouts and degraded-mode behavior.
PR fixing telemetry query timeouts, adding retries/backoff, and improving error messages in bot cards.
PR in redwood monorepo exporting deploy metadata (service/version/rollout status) via an internal endpoint or event stream.
PR adding a tenant-aware config diff endpoint with authorization checks and redaction hooks.
PR adding scheduler saturation metrics (queue depth, backpressure, admission control) to the metrics pipeline.
PR adding safe tenant-aware metric query primitives used by diagnostics tooling and Console deep links.
PR emitting audit log events whenever incident-bot accesses config diffs or privileged telemetry endpoints.
PR wiring role/scopes into config diff access with a break-glass flow for on-call during Sev0/Sev1 incidents.
PR adding rate limits and circuit breakers for diagnostics endpoints to prevent self-inflicted load during incidents.
Hotfix PR reducing metric cardinality from fallback-routing tags after an incident where dashboards slowed down.
PR adding standardized dashboards aligned to incident-bot context cards (deploy timeline, saturation overview, error budget burn).
PR tuning alerts around GPU saturation and queue depth to reduce paging noise while preserving early warning signals.
PR adding log correlation shortcuts (trace/log deep links) referenced by the bot for faster drill-down.
PR generating error budget burn URLs (per service/route/region) for embedding in incident-bot and runbooks.
PR adding an incident timeline export format to support postmortems and automated context attachments.
PR updating internal/external docs with incident-bot v2 operator guidance and troubleshooting steps.
PR adding a perf canary that monitors telemetry query latency to ensure bot context gathering remains fast under load.
Thread during a production incident where responders note missing deploy context and propose adding deploy metadata to the bot.
On-call brainstorm thread enumerating must-have signals (deploys/config diffs/saturation) and mapping to current gaps.
SRE thread discussing MTTR baseline, how to measure improvement, and what to instrument for context completeness.
Platform thread debating config diff endpoint authorization model, redaction, and audit logging requirements.
Release engineering thread aligning on deploy metadata schema and how to link deploys to PRs and rollout phases.
Architecture review thread with feedback on data flow, caching, rate limiting, and failure behavior under partial outages.
Infra/SRE coordination thread on bounding diagnostics load (rate limits, circuit breakers, backoff) to avoid cascading failures.
Discussion comparing GPU util vs queue depth vs KV cache pressure, and what thresholds should trigger incident-bot highlights.
Incident thread where responders struggle to correlate streaming timeouts with deploy/config; leads to action items for bot v2.
Thread assigning postmortem action items related to deploy context and config diff visibility in incident response.
Thread planning feature flags, cohort targeting, and rollback criteria for rolling out bot v2 safely.
SRE thread selecting beta cohort and defining what feedback to capture during the first rotation using bot v2.
On-call feedback on card format (too verbose/too sparse), proposed truncation rules, and preferred deep links.
Incident thread focused on regional saturation; highlights need for consistent saturation signals and routing/fallback context.
Thread agreeing on which dashboards the bot should link to and how to parameterize links per service/region/tenant.
Thread troubleshooting missing service mapping for deploy events and deciding on a canonical service registry lookup.
Thread coordinating bot OAuth/service identity scopes and ensuring audit events are emitted for privileged operations.
Thread after a telemetry query latency spike; discusses caching, query budgets, and fallback-to-links behavior.
Incident thread where config diff would have sped up triage; responders manually hunt for feature-flag changes.
Thread listing runbooks that must be updated before broad rollout and assigning doc owners.
Thread reviewing redaction rules for config diffs and agreeing on an allowlist plus tests to prevent leakage.
Thread specifying how bot should behave when upstream services are unhealthy (timeouts, cached context, “manual steps” snippet).
Thread defining a “context completeness” score (deploy/config/saturation present) and how to log it for analysis.
Incident thread where early bot v2 beta output helps responders quickly identify saturation and recent deploy correlation.
Beta retro thread: what cards were helpful, what was noisy, and what to change before GA.
Thread scheduling GA rollout window and defining backout steps if bot changes cause confusion or added load.
Announcement thread communicating incident-bot v2 GA, key changes, and where to file issues/feedback.
Help thread troubleshooting empty context cards (permissions missing, telemetry query timeout) with steps to resolve.
Customer support ticket for a Dedicated customer reporting latency spikes; investigation references need for standardized saturation signals and bot context.
Support ticket where a routing policy/config change caused elevated 503s; includes request for safer config diff visibility during incidents.
Support ticket for streaming disconnects correlated with a deploy; resolution notes include improved deploy context surfacing and deep links.
Internal helpdesk ticket: incident-bot lacking required scope/role in prod; tracked as a permissions/audit logging fix.
Internal ticket documenting telemetry query timeouts caused by bot bursts; leads to caching/rate limit work and a perf canary.
Leadership email thread aligning on MTTR targets, rollout risk management, and resourcing across SRE/platform/telemetry; includes exec asks and deadlines.
Email thread with platform/security stakeholders approving the permissioning + audit approach for config diff and privileged telemetry access.
Product/engineering coordination email on Console deep-link requirements and ensuring links land on the right service/region/time window during incidents.
Technical deep dive transcript with a large customer after an incident; discusses what context they needed (deploy/config/saturation) and planned improvements.
Private deployment technical deep dive transcript focused on day-2 ops expectations (audit logs, incident diagnostics, SLO reporting) that reinforces internal requirements.
